form.2. SHORT COURSE DESCRIPTION: This course examines modern AI-native software development, where developers collaborate with increasingly capable coding agents. It covers how to define intent, provide effective context, structure development workflows, and coordinate AI tools. Students gain practical experience designing and evaluating agent-assisted software development processes.
form.3. TOPICS / CONTENT AREAS:
Treatment of this list: starting hypotheses — may add/drop/reorder with justification
A. AI-Native Development: AI-assisted coding, coding agents, developer workflows

B. Agentic Software Engineering: MCP, agent skills, tool use, context engineering

C. Specification & Planning: spec-driven development, requirements to executable specifications

D. Software Development Workflows: loop engineering, iterative development, software factories

E. Engineering Practice: automated testing, evaluation, deployment, reliability

F. Practical Development: hands-on coding, projects, emerging developer tools
form.4. COURSE INTENT:
Central question the course answers: How can software developers effectively
design and operate development workflows in which humans and AI agents
collaboratively build reliable software?

Pedagogical emphasis: Practical, workflow-oriented understanding through
hands-on development and experimentation.

This course should NOT become:
- A general introduction to AI or machine learning
- A traditional programming course
- A purely theoretical treatment of large language models

existence.reason: While CSE701 covers AI in Software Engineering with an overlap of 0.185 (which is above the substantial threshold of 0.15), CSE701 focuses broadly on data and research literature in software engineering, whereas the new course specifically targets modern AI-native software development workflows, coding agents, and human-AI collaborative execution.
existence.recommendation: Proceed as a distinct course offering focusing on practical AI-native development workflows and agentic engineering.

overlaps.differentiation: CSE701 examines data-driven software engineering and research literature, whereas the new course focuses on operationalizing AI coding agents, developer workflows, and agentic engineering practices.

CSE594A focuses primarily on agentic reasoning for algorithmic and mathematical problem-solving, whereas this course applies agentic systems specifically to software development workflows and engineering practice.
CSE582 addresses traditional software product lines, maintenance, and re-engineering, whereas the new course investigates AI-driven software factories and generative workflow automation.
CSE581 covers cognitive perspectives and traditional/agile systems analysis, whereas the new course focuses on AI-native specification and execution.
AI501 provides foundational machine learning theory and modeling, whereas this course assumes ML capability and applies AI tools to software engineering workflows.
CSE201 teaches foundational advanced programming and manual unit testing in Java, whereas the new course deals with automated agentic testing and loop engineering.
CSE583 focuses on open-source software and tools, whereas this course focuses on AI-native development.
CSE665 covers foundational transformer architectures and LLM training principles, whereas this course applies existing models to software workflows.

narrative.course_description: This course examines modern AI-native software development, where developers collaborate with coding agents. It covers how to configure agent skills and tool use protocols, translate requirements into executable specifications, analyze execution traces from automated agent workflows, and assess pipelines integrating automated testing and reliability checks. Students will be able to configure agent skills and tool use protocols using an orchestration framework, translate natural language requirements into executable specifications, analyze execution traces to identify failure causes, and assess AI-native development pipelines. The course is taught through lectures, tutorials, and laboratory sessions emphasizing hands-on project work and developer workflows.
narrative.sequencing_rationale: The modules progress from foundational agent orchestration and tool use to spec-driven development, log analysis of automated agent workflows, and finally pipeline assessment and reliability checks. This sequence builds upon the mandatory prerequisite knowledge of advanced programming and automated testing from CSE201.
narrative.assessment_rationale: The assessment mix comprising quizzes, assignments, projects, mid-semester, and end-semester examinations aligns with the course outcomes by combining theoretical understanding with practical, hands-on evaluation of agent-assisted software development processes, projects, and pipeline reliability.
narrative.positioning_rationale: This course differs from CSE701, which emphasizes data-driven software engineering and research literature, and CSE594A, which focuses on agentic reasoning for algorithmic problem-solving, by specifically targeting operationalized AI coding agents, developer workflows, and agentic software engineering practices.
